chunks: It was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father,
that Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a pot that had been set to cook, and lo, there was a mouse in the pot. He said: "Its broth is to be poured out, the meat washed, and it is to be eaten."
For the meaning of this report is: when it [the mouse] dies in it [the pot], discarding the pot's contents becomes obligatory.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia Islam when a mouse is found dead in a cooking pot?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) was asked about a cooking pot that had been set to cook and in which a mouse was then discovered. He ruled that its broth must be poured out, the meat washed, and then consumed. Shaykh al-Tusi appends an editorial clarification explaining that the specific obligation to discard the pot's contents applies only when the mouse has died inside it — distinguishing this case from the chapter's general subject of an animal that falls in water and exits alive.
